answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a bonded reputation vine: every agent stakes a deposit that grows only through verified work, and its standing travels along an atlas of endorsements from peers who have staked and delivered themselves. Fresh fake identities buy no history, since new accounts start with zero endorsements and cannot mint reputation. Dormant identities help no one either: trust decays without ongoing real work, so a relic account cannot be revived and sold as credibility. Attackers must fund productive agents, costing as much as honest participation.
